# Eval Contract Checklist: Large-phase remeasure

**Purpose**: Requirements quality of the remeasure as a release contract — measurement validity,
usage attribution, comparability across arms, and the outcome — before `/speckit-tasks`
**Created**: 2026-10-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md),
[contracts/harness.md](../contracts/harness.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

Depth: formal release gate. Audience: the reviewer of the feature's pull request.

## Measurement validity: the fixture

- [x] CHK001 - Is "6 to 10 tasks" per story phase stated so a reviewer can count it, including whether test-writing tasks count as tasks? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, US1]
- [x] CHK002 - Is the number of user stories in the new fixture fixed ("at least three") consistently between the spec, plan and research? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Research §R5]
- [x] CHK003 - Are the sources of difficulty that are allowed (interacting rules, stated edge cases, multi-module phases) and forbidden (omitted or ambiguous requirements) defined precisely enough to judge a fixture against? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Clarifications]
- [x] CHK004 - Is it specified who judges that a held-out test "tests nothing the spec does not state", and how that judgement is recorded? [Measurability, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK005 - Is the traceability of each held-out test to its acceptance scenario required in a form a reviewer can read (a name, a docstring, a table)? [Gap, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK006 - Is the reference implementation's role defined as proving the oracle only, with a requirement that it is never visible to an arm? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, US1 scenario 3]
- [x] CHK007 - Are the requirements for keeping 001's fixture runnable stated with what "still runs" means (same results expected, or only that the harness accepts it)? [Clarity, Spec US1 scenario 4]
- [x] CHK008 - Is it specified that the new fixture's `CLAUDE.md` rules are identical to 001's, so the review-per-story baseline is comparable? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001]

## Measurement validity: runs, gate and verdict

- [x] CHK009 - Is the median defined for the case where a run's held-out total differs between runs (e.g., a collection error), so medians compare like with like? [Edge Case, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK010 - Is the gate's condition ("at least one `without` run misses at least one held-out test") stated identically in the spec, research and quickstart? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Clarifications]
- [x] CHK011 - Is it defined what happens to `without` runs already counted when the fixture is hardened (discarded), and is that consistent across FR-003 and the edge cases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK012 - Is the stopping condition after two hardenings defined as an outcome the README records, or only as a hand-off to the owner? [Gap, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK013 - Are SC-001's inputs defined unambiguously — total cost including every model, the median of each arm, compared as `1 - with/without`? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK014 - Is the treatment of a tie at exactly 30% specified? [Edge Case, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK015 - Is SC-002's suite clause ("green at the end of every run") reconciled with judging held-out results on the median — is one red suite in three a fail? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK016 - Are SC-003 to SC-007, inherited from 001, stated as applying to every counted run or to some aggregate across the three? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-003–SC-007]
- [x] CHK017 - Is the reporting of spread (min and max) required for both cost and held-out results, and is it stated that spread informs the reading but does not decide the verdict? [Clarity, Clarifications, Research §R7]
- [x] CHK018 - Is the rationale for three runs (rather than more) recorded with the trade-off it accepts, so a reader knows how far a median of three can be trusted? [Assumption, Clarifications]

## Usage attribution

- [x] CHK019 - Is "reconciled" defined with exact tolerances for tokens (equal) and cost (within $0.000001) in the spec or contract a reviewer reads? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008, Contract usage.py]
- [x] CHK020 - Are the phase boundaries (start at the worker call with the phase heading, end at the `tasks: mark phase <n>` commit) specified in the spec or only in research? [Traceability, Spec US2 scenario 2, Research §R4]
- [x] CHK021 - Is the attribution of fix hand-offs and reviews inside a phase's span specified? [Completeness, Research §R4]
- [x] CHK022 - Is the case of a missing transcript defined consistently — counted but unattributed — across the contract, data model and SC-008? [Consistency, Contract run.sh, Spec §SC-008]
- [x] CHK023 - Is it specified what the `without` and `fallback` arms' attribution contains, given core offers no phase boundary? [Completeness, Research §R4, Spec US2]
- [x] CHK024 - Is the price source required to be recorded with its date, and is a model with no known price defined as unreconciled rather than estimated? [Completeness, Contract usage.py]
- [x] CHK025 - Is the dependency on Claude Code's internal transcript format stated as an assumption with its check (reconciliation per run)? [Assumption, Research §R1, §R3]
- [x] CHK026 - Is it specified whether SC-008's failure on a run blocks the release, or only the attribution's use in the reading? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-008]

## Comparability across arms

- [x] CHK027 - Is the set of `versions.txt` keys that must match across arms defined, including the new `fixture` and `arm` keys and which ones are exempt? [Clarity, Contract compare.py, Data model]
- [x] CHK028 - Is the run order (`without` ×3, then `with`/`fallback` alternating) a requirement in the spec, or only a plan decision, and is its reason recorded? [Traceability, Research §R8]
- [x] CHK029 - Is the rule for raising the deadline stated with what happens to runs already counted under the old deadline? [Completeness, Spec Edge Cases, Quickstart]
- [x] CHK030 - Is it specified that no comparison is made against 001's numbers, only within this feature's arms? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK031 - Is the requirement that the probes pass before the eval stated with what happens when one fails (the eval stops)? [Completeness, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK032 - Are reruns of a run that does not count bounded (at most twice) and counted towards that bound when forced by a versions mismatch, as in 001? [Consistency, Spec US3 scenario 3]

## Outcome: release or not adopted

- [x] CHK033 - Are the artifacts that must agree on a release (`preset.yml` version, CHANGELOG, tag) and their semantic version (a first release's number) specified? [Gap, Spec US3 scenario 1, Constitution V]
- [x] CHK034 - Is the README entry's required content listed completely enough to review against (001's fields plus attribution, runs, spread, gate history, hardening)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, US3]
- [x] CHK035 - Is the not-adopted path's record defined, including what "with its reason" must name (which criterion, by how much, and what the attribution shows)? [Clarity, Spec US3 scenario 2]
- [x] CHK036 - Is the owner's spend confirmation defined with what it shows (spent so far, estimate) and how the estimate is derived? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK037 - Is the adoption step after a release (001's FR-013) referenced in a way that stays valid if 001's spec is not read, or does 002 depend on it implicitly? [Dependency, Spec §FR-010, US4]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Reviewed 2026-10-14 by two fresh-context reviews: the first found 19 items not met and 5 uncovered
  contradictions, all fixed in the documents; the second found CHK004 and CHK020 not met and 14
  uncovered gaps, fixed in turn. A third review found all 37 items met (CHK004 and CHK020 included)
  and 14 new gaps, fixed by the spec's FR-013 refinements, SC-004's core-skill wording and the
  `runs.sh` driver (research R11).
- CHK022 and CHK032 were judged against the design as it now stands: a run without reconciled usage
  is not counted (not "counted but unattributed"), and a pre-run versions mismatch refuses the try
  without using a rerun. A fourth review (2026-10-14) found two blockers and twelve smaller gaps,
  all fixed in the documents.
